knowledge-base.overview: Framework guardrails, patterns, and best practices for Django 5+. Loaded automatically when agents work on Django projects. Applies to Django REST Framework, Django Channels, Python 3.10+.

core-principles.principle: Leverage Django's built-in features before adding third-party packages. Django ships with auth, admin, ORM, CSRF, and more.
Don't Repeat Yourself — use abstract models, mixins, and shared utilities.
Keep business logic in models and services, not views. Views handle HTTP, nothing else.
Use clear URL patterns, explicit imports, named relationships.
CSRF, XSS protection, SQL injection prevention are built in — do not disable them.

good-fit.item: Admin interface needed out of the box

guardrail.rule: Never hardcode SECRET_KEY. Use python-decouple or environment variables. Hardcoded secrets will leak in version control.
guardrail.good: from decouple import config SECRET_KEY = config("SECRET_KEY")

guardrail.rule: Never use raw SQL with string formatting. The ORM uses parameterized queries. If raw SQL is required, use cursor.execute("SELECT ... WHERE id = %s", [user_id]).
Never use |safe template filter with user-provided data. Django templates auto-escape by default; |safe disables this protection.
Always define AUTH_USER_MODEL before the first migration. Changing it afterward requires data migrations and schema changes.
Always use select_related() for ForeignKey/OneToOne and prefetch_related() for ManyToMany/reverse FK. Never allow N+1 queries in views or serializers.
Use @transaction.atomic for multi-step writes. A failure mid-way must not leave the database in a partial state.
Never use CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = True in production. Use explicit CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list.
Never call Model.objects.all() without pagination or a limit. Unbounded queries can load millions of rows.
Always define __str__ on every model. Without it, admin and debug output show unhelpful object representations.
Use TextChoices/IntegerChoices for status fields. Never use raw strings or integers for enumerable values.

project-structure.note: Split settings into base.py, dev.py, prod.py. Group apps under apps/. Place business logic in services.py, not in views.

pattern.name: Abstract Base Models
Custom User Model
pattern.description: Always create a custom user model before the first migration. Extend AbstractUser (not AbstractBaseUser unless full control is needed).
pattern.example:
# apps/users/models.py from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser from django.db import models from apps.core.models import TimeStampedModel, UUIDModel
class User(AbstractUser, UUIDModel, TimeStampedModel): email = models.EmailField(unique=True) USERNAME_FIELD = "email" REQUIRED_FIELDS = ["username"]
class Meta: db_table = "users" ordering = ["-created_at"] indexes = [models.Index(fields=["email"])]
def __str__(self) -> str: return self.email

pattern.name: Class-Based Views
Avoiding N+1 Queries
Atomic Transactions
pattern.example:
from django.db import transaction
@transaction.atomic def transfer_stock(source_id, dest_id, qty): source = Product.objects.select_for_update().get(id=source_id) dest = Product.objects.select_for_update().get(id=dest_id) source.stock -= qty dest.stock += qty source.save(update_fields=["stock"]) dest.save(update_fields=["stock"])

settings-checklist.item: Never hardcode SECRET_KEY — use python-decouple or environment variables
Always define AUTH_USER_MODEL before first migration

model-checklist.item: Always set class Meta with db_table, ordering, and indexes
Use abstract base models for shared fields (TimeStampedModel, UUIDModel)
Use TextChoices/IntegerChoices for status fields (not raw strings)
Add related_name to all ForeignKey and OneToOneField relationships
Use on_delete explicitly: CASCADE, PROTECT, SET_NULL, SET_DEFAULT
Add database indexes for frequently queried fields

security-checklist.item: CSRF: Enabled by default for forms; use @csrf_exempt sparingly
XSS: Django templates auto-escape by default; never use |safe with user data
SQL Injection: ORM uses parameterized queries; never use raw SQL with string formatting
Clickjacking: X-Frame-Options middleware enabled by default
HTTPS: Set SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True in production
Cookies: Set SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
CORS: Use django-cors-headers with explicit allowed origins (never CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS in production)

rules.rule: Use pytest with pytest-django (not Django's built-in test runner)
Use factory-boy or fixtures for test data
Use APIClient for DRF endpoint testing
Test file naming: test_models.py, test_views.py, test_services.py

quick-reference.item: python-decouple config() or os.environ; never hardcode
select_related() for FK/O2O; prefetch_related() for M2M/reverse FK
@transaction.atomic for multi-step writes; select_for_update() for locking
Always AUTH_USER_MODEL before first migration; extend AbstractUser
Never all() without limits; use only()/defer() for partial columns
ModelViewSet for CRUD; thin endpoints, logic in services.py
|safe never with user data; CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS never in prod
__str__ always; class Meta always; TextChoices for enums
base/dev/prod split; ALLOWED_HOSTS explicit; HTTPS flags in prod
